classification.difficultyReason: Find the common target sum and connect equal-sum number groups to regions that two straight cuts can actually form on the clock.

content.prompt: Using two straight lines, divide the clock face into three parts so that the sums of the numbers in each part are equal.

spec.description: Unshaded circular clock with numerals 1–12 in conventional positions, a centre point and no hands. Decorative rim and face shading are omitted; the centre marker uses ordinary black ink.
spec.mathematics: Twelve numerals in clockwise order; two student-drawn straight lines must produce three equal-sum regions.
spec.answerVisibility: No partition lines or answers are supplied.

answer.short: Separate $11,12,1,2$ from $10,9,3,4$, and separate $10,9,3,4$ from $8,7,6,5$, using the two lines shown. Each region sums to $26$.
answer.worked:
The twelve numbers total $78$, so each of the three regions must sum to $78\div3=26$. Draw one straight line between 10 and 11 and between 2 and 3. Draw the other between 8 and 9 and between 4 and 5.

$$\begin{align*}11+12+1+2&=26\\10+9+3+4&=26\\8+7+6+5&=26\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Complete clock with two parallel descending straight partition lines, separating the same numeral groups as the teacher diagram.
spec.mathematics: Regions contain {11,12,1,2}, {10,9,3,4} and {8,7,6,5}; each sum is 26.
